1:0: Bayt al-Ahzan: on the circumstances of the Mistress of the Women of the Worlds, Fatima al-Zahra, peace be upon her. By the venerable shaykh, the discerning traditionist, al-Hajj al-Shaykh 'Abbas al-Qummi, may his resting place be made sweet.
2:0: The book: Bayt al-Ahzan. The author: al-Hajj al-Shaykh 'Abbas al-Qummi, may God have mercy upon him. The edition: the first of the new printing. Publisher: Dar al-Hikma. Press: Amir. Rabi' al-Thani 1412 AH.
3:0: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. We praise You, O You who made the love of Muhammad the Prophet and his Family — peace be upon him and upon them — and enmity towards their enemies a pillar of the religion, a support of faith and certainty, and a means of deliverance from the humiliating punishment. So convey and deliver the best of Your blessings and Your peace upon them all, for ever and ever; and curse and chastise their enemies, the Nasibis who deny them.
3:1: To proceed: since the book Bayt al-Ahzan, on the afflictions of the Mistress of Women — God's blessings be upon her, and upon her father, her husband and her sons — being among the writings of the servant of the People of the House, peace be upon them, the treasure of the traditionists and the last of them, al-Hajj al-Shaykh 'Abbas al-Qummi, may God envelop him in His forgiveness — is a valuable, comprehensive and beneficial book on its subject, arranged in four chapters and thirty-two sections: the virtuous, sincere and diligent promoter of the scholars' legacy, Taqi b. al-Mahdi, known as al-'Allama, director of the Dar al-Hikma institute — may God increase him in His enabling grace — undertook to print and publish it anew, and asked me to devote my effort to verifying the book, correcting it, and tracing its sources. Despite my inadequacy for that, I answered his request. I offer him my thanks for the favour he has shown me, and I ask God to grant me guidance, success and acceptance, and the revival of the legacy of the Messenger and his Family, peace be upon them.
4:0: Since the book, in both its old and its new printing, contained many errors, I collated its hadiths against their original sources, or against the large hadith and historical encyclopaedias. Wherever there was a difference in wording — an addition or an omission — I noted it in the margin, and placed some of it between brackets [ ]. I have also explained the meanings of difficult words, drawing on the Bihar of al-'Allama al-Majlisi, may God have mercy on him, and on other eminent scholars.
4:1: I ask the scholars who examine this book to favour me with correction and sound criticism wherever a slip or an error has, on rare occasion, occurred.
4:2: In closing, I offer abundant thanks and ample praise to his eminence Hujjat al-Islam wa'l-Muslimin al-Shaykh Mustafa al-Harandi for the great kindness he expended in reviewing this valuable book and tracing its sources; for he presented to us, in all sincerity, the work he had completed on this precious volume before ever we began. How excellent is he, and his reward rests with God.
4:3: May God deal with them all in His kindness, and gather them on the Day of Resurrection with Muhammad and the infallible People of his House, peace be upon them.
4:4: And I am the sinful servant, Muhammad, known as Durudi al-Tafrishi.
5:0: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Praise belongs to God, before whom the necks of tyrants are humbled and to whom the necks of the Chosroes bow. And may God bless the noblest of His creation and the most excellent of His creatures, Abu al-Qasim al-Mustafa Muhammad, and the People of his House, the good, the pure, the infallible — and above all the Remnant of God in the earths, al-Hujja b. al-Hasan al-'Askari, may God hasten his noble relief.
5:1: And may the curse rest upon their enemies, their opponents, those who defy them, those who usurped their rights, those who deny their virtues and their merits, and all who lay claim to their stations and their ranks — from now until the Day of Judgement arrives. Amen, Lord of the Worlds.
5:2: The eminence of the author: he is al-'Allama al-Hajj al-Shaykh 'Abbas b. Muhammad Rida b. Abi al-Qasim al-Qummi. His eminence and his renown among the elite and the common people alike — for knowledge and practice, for asceticism and scrupulousness, for love of the People of the House of Revelation, upon whom be the most excellent blessings of those who bless, for his abundant narration from them, for his pride in walking their path, for his proclaiming of their virtues, and for his sincerity in most of his affairs and in all of his deeds — is too manifest to be uttered and too well known to be written down. And how should it be otherwise?
6:0: His writings — which are the fairest witness and the most truthful speaker — attest to that. For there is scarcely a household among the Imami Shi'a in which one of his valuable works is not to be found; at the very least his book al-Mafatih, which is present in every one of the noble shrines, and that is a truthful witness to his devotion to those buried in them, peace be upon them.
6:1: That being so, this narrow space does not permit us to set out all his circumstances or to record his qualities in full. We refer whoever desires that to its proper place in the books of biography, and we counsel our non-Arab brethren to read the book composed in Persian on the author's life, entitled Hajj Shaykh 'Abbas Qummi: a man of virtue and piety, which is among the writings of al-Shaykh 'Ali Dawani — and in it, together with his noble likeness, are specimens of his beautiful hand.
6:2: In conclusion, we content ourselves in this introduction with recording all the writings of the author of this book, arranged in alphabetical order.
7:0: An index of the writings of the traditionist al-Qummi, may God's good pleasure be upon him, arranged in alphabetical order, together with what we have drawn from his book named al-Fawa'id al-Radawiyya. The noble scholar and venerable traditionist — reviver of the sacred law by his writings, publisher of the truths of the Shi'a by his compositions, who clung to the skirts of the pure Family, upon whom be the blessings of the Majestic and All-Knowing Sovereign, and of whom it deserves to be said that he is among the good things of the age and the blessings of the time — al-Hajj al-Shaykh 'Abbas b. Muhammad Rida b. Abi al-Qasim al-Qummi, may God gather them with the Prophet and his Family, God's blessings be upon them all — said in his book entitled al-Fawa'id al-Radawiyya fi ahwal 'ulama' al-madhhab al-Ja'fariyya, which is among his valuable works in the Persian language and which the traditionist, may God have mercy on him, composed in the precinct of the holy and purified Radawi shrine, where, in giving an account of himself, he wrote what is rendered here into Arabic: Since this noble book is an exposition of the circumstances of the scholars, I did not think it fitting or proper to include an account of myself in it, for I am too lowly and too slight to be counted in their number, that my own circumstances should be entered among theirs. I therefore turn from that and content myself with mentioning my writings. My birth was, to all appearance, in the year 1294 AH; and my writings up to now — the present year being 1333 AH, my age having reached about forty years — fall into four parts:
8:0: Part One: the books that have been printed and circulated.
8:1: Part Two: the books that have been written out for the press and will be printed shortly. (It will not escape the noble reader that these books were printed thereafter and circulated.)
8:2: Part Three: the books whose composition I have completed, but which at present no one is undertaking to print.
8:3: (It will not escape the noble reader that some of them were printed and then circulated.)
8:4: Part Four: the books whose composition has not been completed; I ask God Most High to favour me with the enabling grace to complete them.
8:5: (It will not escape the noble reader that the venerable traditionist said afterwards: most of these books of unfinished composition have been lost.)
8:6: The number of the writings of the venerable traditionist al-Qummi, may God's good pleasure be upon him, reached — as he himself stated — seventy books, between small and large, amounting in all to seventy-four volumes; and he further translated books from Arabic into Persian and from Persian into Arabic. He composed all these many valuable works without his noble life exceeding forty years. What follows is a register of the titles of his writings, which we have arranged alphabetically so that it may be consulted more easily; in it we have included both what he mentioned in al-Fawa'id al-Radawiyya and what he composed after that book. Alif: 1 — Al-Anwar al-Bahiyya, on the history of the Prophet and his Family, peace be upon them; one volume, in Arabic; printed.
8:7: 2 — Al-Ayat al-Bayyinat, on the reports of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, concerning the trials to come and things unseen; he did not complete it.
8:8: Ba': 3 — Bayt al-Ahzan fi masa'ib sayyidat al-niswan; Arabic; printed — and it is this book.
9:0: 4 — Al-Baqiyat al-Salihat, in the margin of Mafatih al-Jinan; Persian; printed repeatedly together with the Mafatih.
9:1: Ta': 5 — Tuhfa Tusiyya wa nafha qudsiyya, also called Risala Mashhad-nama.
9:2: (Persian; printed. It is a short work explaining the construction of the Radawi shrine, upon its occupant be peace, and mentioning its buildings and the places connected with it, together with a number of important and reliable ziyarat.)
9:3: 6 — Tatimmat al-Muntaha, on the events of the days of the caliphs; Persian; it is the third volume of his book Muntaha al-Amal; printed.
9:4: 7 — Tuhfat al-Ahbab fi nawadir al-ashab — on the circumstances of the Companions of the Greatest Messenger, may God bless him and his Family, and of the companions of the Imams, peace be upon them; printed.
9:5: 8 — A translation of Misbah al-Mutahajjid of al-Shaykh al-Tusi, may God have mercy on him, into Persian; printed together with the Misbah.
9:6: 9 — A translation of Jamal al-Usbu' of al-Sayyid b. Tawus, may God have mercy on him, into Persian; printed together with Jamal al-Usbu'.
9:7: 10 — A translation of the second course of the book al-Malhuf of al-Sayyid b. Tawus, may God have mercy on him, into Persian; printed in the margin of al-Malhuf.
9:8: 11 — A translation of Zad al-Ma'ad of al-'Allama al-Majlisi, may God have mercy on him, into Arabic; it appears to be incomplete.
9:9: 12 — A translation of Tuhfat al-Za'ir of al-'Allama al-Majlisi, may God have mercy on him, into Arabic; it appears to be likewise incomplete.
9:10: 13 — Tatmim Tahiyyat al-Za'ir, of his teacher the traditionist al-Nuri, may God have mercy on him; printed.
9:11: 14 — Tatmim Bidayat al-Hidaya, of al-Shaykh al-Hurr al-'Amili, may God have mercy on him; in manuscript. Perhaps it is the book known as Fasl wa Wasl, which he detached from al-Shaykh Hurr al-'Amili and joined to the traditionist
10:0: al-Qummi, may God have mercy on him. Jim: 15 — Chihil Hadith (Forty Hadiths); in Persian; printed several times in Iran.
10:1: Ha': 16 — Hikma Baligha wa mi'at kalima jami'a, a Persian commentary on a hundred of the sayings of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him; printed repeatedly in Iran.
10:2: Dal: 17 — Al-Durra al-Yatima fi tatimmat al-durra al-thamina, a completion of the commentary on al-Nisab by al-Fadil al-Yazdi (printed). 18 — Dastur al-'Ilm (printed).
10:3: 19 — Al-Durr al-Nazim fi lughat al-Qur'an al-'Azim (printed).
10:4: 20 — Davazdah Ad'iya-yi Ma'thura (Twelve Transmitted Supplications); Persian; printed repeatedly together with Chihil Hadith.
10:5: Dhal: 21 — Dhakhirat al-'Uqba fi mathalib a'da' al-Zahra, peace be upon her; not completed.
10:6: 22 — Dhakhirat al-Abrar fi muntakhab Anis al-Tujjar; not completed.
10:7: Sin: 23 — Sabil al-Rashad fi usul al-din (printed).
10:8: 24 — Safinat Bihar al-Anwar wa madinat al-hikam wa'l-athar, in two volumes; Arabic; printed repeatedly in Iran and elsewhere. It is a subject index to the book Bihar al-Anwar of al-'Allama al-Majlisi, may God have mercy on him.
11:0: Shin: 25 — A commentary on the Wajiza of Shaykh al-Baha'i, upon whom be mercy, on the science of hadith criticism.
11:1: 26 — A commentary on the short sayings of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, which al-Sayyid Radi al-Din, may God have mercy on him, placed at the end of his book Nahj al-Balagha (incomplete). 27 — A commentary on al-Sahifa al-Sajjadiyya (incomplete).
11:2: 28 — A commentary on forty hadiths; in manuscript and unfinished; a copy of it survives.
11:3: Sad: 29 — Saha'if al-Nur, on the acts of the days, the year and the months (incomplete). Dad: 30 — Diyafat al-Ikhwan (incomplete).
11:4: Ta': 31 — Tabaqat al-Rijal. It appears to be the book of the classes of the caliphs, the companions of the Imams, peace be upon them, the scholars and the poets, printed at the end of Tatimmat al-Muntaha in Persian.
11:5: 'Ayn: 32 — 'Ilm al-Yaqin, an abridgement of Haqq al-Yaqin of al-'Allama al-Majlisi, may God have mercy on him.
11:6: Ghayn: 33 — Ghayat al-Quswa, a translation of al-'Urwa al-Wuthqa of the late jurist al-Sayyid Muhammad Kazim al-Yazdi, may his secret be sanctified, in two volumes: the first from the beginning of the Book of Purity to the rulings concerning the dead, and the second from the Book of Prayer to the discussion of covering and the coverer (Persian; printed).
12:0: Fa': 34 — Al-Fawa'id al-Rajabiyya, on what pertains to the Arabic months (comprising the events of the days, and containing a number of the acts of the months. This is the first of his compositions, may God have mercy on him, as he states in al-Fawa'id al-Radawiyya, adding that a manuscript in his own noble hand was in his keeping).
12:2: 36 — Al-Fawa'id al-Radawiyya fi ahwal 'ulama' al-madhhab al-Ja'fariyya (printed).
12:3: 37 — Fayd al-'Allam, on what pertains to the months and the days.
12:4: 38 — Fayd al-Qadir, on what pertains to the hadith of Ghadir (a condensation of two large volumes of the book 'Abaqat al-Anwar of al-Sayyid Hamid Husayn al-Hindi al-Nishaburi, may God perfume his noble grave, on the hadith of Ghadir). 39 — Al-Fawa'id al-Tusiyya, which is a miscellany.
12:5: Qaf: 40 — Qurrat al-Basira fi ta'rikh al-hujaj al-tahira.
12:6: Kaf: 41 — Al-Kuna wa'l-Alqab, in three volumes; printed; Arabic.
12:7: 42 — Al-Kuna wa'l-Alqab, a short abridgement (printed). 43 — Kalimat Latifa (printed).
12:8: 44 — Kuhl al-Basar fi sirat sayyid al-bashar (printed).
12:9: Kaf: 45 — Gunahan-i Kabira wa Saghira, on the greater and lesser sins (printed; in Persian).
13:0: Lam: 46 — Al-La'ali al-Manthura fi al-ahraz wa'l-adhkar al-ma'thura (printed).
13:1: Mim: 47 — Mukhtasar al-Abwab fi al-sunan wa'l-adab (a condensation of the book Hilyat al-Muttaqin of al-'Allama al-Majlisi, may God have mercy on him, in Persian); printed.
13:2: 48 — Mafatih al-Jinan, on supplications and ziyarat; Persian; printed repeatedly. It is among the most famous of his books and the most beneficial to people at large, elite and common alike, and it has been rendered into various languages; I have seen it thus far rendered into Arabic and translated into Urdu.
13:3: 49 — Manazil al-Akhira wa al-matalib al-fakhira, on the states of the barzakh and the stations of the Resurrection; Persian; printed.
13:4: 50 — Maqamat-i 'Aliyya, an abridgement of Mi'raj al-Sa'ada of the godly scholar al-Shaykh al-Mawla Ahmad al-Naraqi; Persian; printed.
13:5: 51 — Muntaha al-Amal fi dhikr masa'ib al-Nabi wa'l-Al, in two volumes; Persian; printed. It too is among the most famous of his books after the Mafatih, and the most beneficial to people at large, elite and common alike.
13:6: 52 — Maqalid al-Falah fi 'amal al-yawm wa'l-layla. 53 — Miqlad al-Najah, an abridgement of the preceding book.
13:7: 54 — An abridgement of the eleventh volume of Bihar al-Anwar of al-'Allama al-Majlisi, may God perfume his noble resting place; lost.
13:8: 55 — An abridgement of al-Shama'il of al-Tirmidhi; lost.
13:9: 56 — Musalli al-Musab bi-faqd al-ikhwa wa'l-ahbab; lost.
13:10: 57 — An abridgement of Dar al-Salam of the traditionist al-Nuri, under the title Ghayat al-Maram fi talkhis Dar al-Salam; lost.
14:0: Nun: 58 — Nafas al-Mahmum wa nafthat al-masdur; Arabic; printed. It is a book on the martyrdom of the Imam Abu 'Abd Allah al-Husayn and his companions, and it has been translated into Persian.
14:1: 59 — Nuzhat al-Nawadir, a translation of Ma'dan al-Jawahir. 60 — Naqd al-Wasa'il, on the chapter of al-Wasa'il; no copy of it is to be found.
14:2: Ha': 61 — Hadiyyat al-Za'irin wa bahjat al-nazirin.
14:3: It comprises the ziyarat of the pure Proofs, peace be upon them, the noble stations, the graves of the scholars that lie within the shrines, the acts of the week, and the acts of the day and the night; printed.
14:4: 62 — Hidayat al-Ahbab fi al-ma'rufin bi'l-kuna wa'l-alqab (printed).
14:5: 63 — Hidayat al-Anam ila waqa'i' al-ayyam, an abridgement of the book Fayd al-'Allam, also among his writings and mentioned above; printed.
15:0: His death, his burial place, and his children. The traditionist al-Qummi, may God raise his degree, died on the night of the twenty-third of Dhu al-Hijja al-Haram in the year 1359 AH.
15:1: He was sixty-five years of age, according to what his son — may he be forgiven — the venerable scholar and dear preacher, beloved of the hearts of elite and common alike, al-Hajj Mirza 'Ali Muhaddith-zada, wrote at the foot of page 222 of the book al-Fawa'id al-Radawiyya.
15:2: He was buried, may God have mercy on him, in the courtyard of the master of those who profess God's oneness, the Commander of the Faithful, the victorious Lion of God, 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon him, in the third portico on the eastern side, beside his great teacher — the godly scholar and devoted traditionist, the shaykh of shaykhs, al-'Allama al-Hajj al-Mirza Husayn al-Nuri, author of Mustadrak al-Wasa'il and of other beneficial books. May God's good pleasure be upon them both, and may He join them and gather them with those they loved, Muhammad and his wronged Family, peace be upon them.
15:3: He left two good sons. One of them has died: the noble scholar and preacher, beloved of the hearts of elite and common alike, who annotated his father's books, al-Hajj Mirza 'Ali Muhaddith-zada; he was buried at the Shaykhan cemetery in Qum. The other is the venerable scholar, his honour Mirza Muhsin Muhaddith-zada, resident in Tehran, may God Most High preserve him. He also left two daughters.
15:4: This is the last of what we intended to set down here. We ask God for pardon and for acceptance, and that He favour us all with the appearance of the Proof, peace be upon him.
16:0: This is the book Bayt al-Ahzan, recounting the circumstances of the Mistress of the Women of the Worlds, the part of the Seal of the Prophets and the mother of the pure Imams; the purest of women, heiress of the master of the prophets and consort of the master of the legatees; the human houri and the virgin Batul, Fatima al-Zahra, God's blessings be upon her.
17:0: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Praise belongs to God, helper of the wronged, breaker of tyrants, destroyer of the oppressors; and blessing and peace upon him whom He sent as a mercy to the worlds, Muhammad, master of the first and of the last, and upon his Family and his kindred, the guides of the worlds.
17:1: To proceed. He who hopes for the pardon of his Lord, the All-Sufficient — 'Abbas b. Muhammad Rida al-Qummi, may God deal with them both in His kindness, the hidden and the manifest — says: This is a brief treatise recounting the circumstances of the Mistress of the Women of the Worlds, the part of the Seal of the Prophets and the mother of the pure Imams; the purest of women, heiress of the master of the prophets, consort of the master of the legatees, the human houri, the virgin Batul, the martyred lady, wronged and overpowered, Fatima al-Zahra — God's blessings be upon her, and upon her father, her husband and her sons, for as long as the green sky overshadows the dusty earth — and recounting the afflictions and sorrows that befell her. I have named it Bayt al-Ahzan fi masa'ib sayyidat al-niswan, and arranged it in chapters with a conclusion.
18:0: Chapter One: on her birth, her names and her kunyas, God's blessings be upon her. Section. Fatima, God's blessings be upon her, was born in Jumada al-Akhira, on the twentieth day of it, in the forty-fifth year from the birth of the Prophet, God's blessings be upon him and his Family — that is, five years after the beginning of his mission — as has been related from the two truthful Imams, peace be upon them. [1] The beginning of Khadija's bearing her, may God be pleased with her, was this: when the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, was taken up to heaven, he ate of the fruits of the Garden, of its fresh dates and its apples, and God Most High turned that to a fluid in his loins. When he came down to the earth he lay with Khadija, and she conceived Fatima, peace be upon her. So Fatima is a human houri. [2]
18:1: Whenever the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, longed for the scent of the Garden, he would smell her, and find in her the scent of the Garden and the scent of the tree of Tuba. For that reason too he would kiss her often — though some of his wives objected to him for it, out of ignorance of the nobility of her station. [3]
18:2: If you should say: the night journey of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, was six months before the migration — and it has been said that it was in the second year of the mission — while the birth of Fatima, peace be upon her, came after it
18:n3: Bihar, vol. 43, p. 5, hadiths 4-5; and also p. 6, hadith 6.
19:0: by three years — how then can the two be reconciled? I say: his ascension, may God bless him and his Family, was not confined to a single occasion, such that the two could not be reconciled. Rather it is related from al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, that he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, was taken up one hundred and twenty times, and on every one of them God, mighty and exalted, enjoined upon the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, devotion to 'Ali and the Imams, peace be upon them, more than He enjoined upon him the obligatory duties. [4]
19:1: Al-'Allama al-Majlisi, may God have mercy on him, said in the Bihar [5]: It has been said: while the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, was sitting at al-Abtah, and with him were 'Ammar b. Yasir, al-Mundhir b. al-Dahdah, Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon him, al-'Abbas b. 'Abd al-Muttalib and Hamza b. 'Abd al-Muttalib, may God have mercy on him, Gabriel, peace be upon him, descended upon him, may God bless him and his Family, in his greatest form, having spread his wings until they reached from the east to the west, and called out to him: O Muhammad, the Most High, the Most Exalted, sends you His greeting, and He commands you to withdraw from Khadija for forty mornings.
19:2: That weighed heavily upon the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, for he loved her and was devoted to her. [6] He said: So the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, remained forty days, fasting by day and rising by night, until, in the last of those days, he sent 'Ammar b. Yasir to Khadija and said: Say to her, O Khadija, do not suppose that my keeping away from you is estrangement or aversion [7]; rather my Lord, mighty and exalted, commanded me to it, that He might carry out His command. So think nothing but good, O Khadija, for God, mighty and exalted, glories in you before His noble angels many times each day.
19:3: And when night falls upon you, shut the door [8] and take your place upon your bed, for I shall be in the house of Fatima bint Asad, may God be pleased with her. And Khadija began to grieve
19:n4: Bihar, vol. 18, p. 387, hadith 96; and also al-Khisal of al-Saduq, p. 566.
19:n8: Ajaftu al-bab: I shut it. In Persian one says: darb ra bar ruy-i khud beband.
20:0: many times each day at the absence of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family.
20:1: When the fortieth day was complete, Gabriel, peace be upon him, descended and said: O Muhammad, the Most High, the Most Exalted, sends you His greeting, and He commands you to make ready for His salutation and His gift.
20:2: The Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, said: O Gabriel, what is the gift of the Lord of the Worlds, and what is His salutation? He said: I have no knowledge of it.
20:3: He said: While the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, was thus, Michael descended, and with him a platter covered with a napkin of fine silk — or he said: of brocade — and set it before the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family. And Gabriel turned to the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, and said: O Muhammad, your Lord commands you to break your fast tonight upon this food.
20:4: 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon him, said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, wished to break his fast, he would order me to open the door to whoever came to break the fast with him. But on that night the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, seated me at the door of the house and said: O son of Abi Talib, this is food forbidden to any but me. 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: So I sat at the door, and the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, was left alone with the food. He uncovered the platter, and there was a cluster (9) of fresh dates and a bunch of grapes.
20:5: The Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, ate of it his fill and drank of the water until satisfied, and stretched out his hand to wash. Gabriel, peace be upon him, poured the water over it, Michael, peace be upon him, washed his hand, and Israfil, peace be upon him, dried it; and what remained of the food rose up with the vessel to heaven.
20:6: Then the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, rose to pray, and Gabriel turned to him and said: Prayer is forbidden to you at this your hour, until you go to the house of Khadija and lie with her; for God, mighty and exalted, has sworn (10) upon Himself that He will create from your loins this night a goodly progeny.
20:7: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, hastened to the house of Khadija.
20:8: (9) Al-'idhq, with kasra: a bunch of grapes or of dates; in Persian it is called khusha. (10) Ala: that is, he swore.
21:0: Khadija, may God's good pleasure be upon her, said: I had grown used to solitude, so that when night fell upon me I would cover my head, let down my curtain [11], bolt my door, pray my portion [12], put out my lamp and take to my bed. On that night I was neither asleep nor fully awake when the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, came and knocked at the door. I called out: Who is this, who knocks at a ring that none knocks at but Muhammad, may God bless him and his Family?
21:1: Khadija said: And the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, called out, with the sweetness of his speech and the pleasantness of his words: Open, O Khadija, for I am Muhammad, may God bless him and his Family.
21:2: Khadija said: I rose, glad and rejoicing at the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, and opened the door, and the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, entered the house. Now when he, may God bless him and his Family, entered the house he would call for the vessel and purify himself for prayer; then he would rise and pray two brief units, and then take to his bed.
21:3: But on that night he did not call for the vessel, nor make ready for prayer. He only took me by the arm and seated me upon his bed, and was tender and playful with me; and there was between me and him what is between a woman and her husband. By Him who raised up the heaven and made the water to gush forth, the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, did not withdraw from me until I felt the weight of Fatima, peace be upon her, within me.
21:4: I say: the Prophet's withdrawal from Khadija, may God be pleased with her, for forty days was in order to make ready for the salutation of the Lord of the Worlds and for His gift — and what is meant by it is Fatima, God's blessings be upon her.
21:5: As is indicated in her ziyara: “And bless the pure Batul” — down to his words: “Fatima, the daughter of Your Messenger, the part of his flesh and the core of his heart, the fruit of his liver, and the salutation from You to him, and the gift.”
21:6: And in this withdrawal is a proof of the eminence of Fatima, Mistress of Women, such as none can bear
21:n11: Asjaftu al-sitr: I let it down.
21:n12: That is, my prayer and my supplication.
22:0: the fingers to set down in writing. Perhaps the singling out of the fresh dates and the grapes was for the abundance of their blessing and the benefits that arise from them, for there is nothing among the trees whose usefulness attains to theirs — and this though the two were created from the remainder of the clay of Adam, peace be upon him. Nor is it far-fetched that in this there is an indication of the abundant benefit of this pure and blessed offspring, and of the multitude of her progeny and her blessings, as we shall hint at, God Most High willing, in its place.
22:1: As for Gabriel's words to the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family — “Prayer is forbidden to you at this your hour” — what appears to be meant is the supererogatory prayer and not the obligatory, for he used to perform it before breaking his fast. God knows best the reality of the matter.
22:2: Al-Shaykh al-Saduq, may God be pleased with him, related in al-Amali, with his chain, from al-Mufaddal b. 'Umar, who said: I said to Abu 'Abd Allah al-Sadiq, peace be upon him: How was the birth of Fatima, peace be upon her? He said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, married Khadija, may God be pleased with her, the women of Mecca shunned her; they would not visit her, nor greet her, nor let any woman visit her. Khadija was made desolate by that, and her distress and her grief were out of fear for him, may God bless him and his Family. Then when she conceived Fatima, peace be upon her, Fatima would speak to her from within her and comfort her; and she kept that hidden from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family.
22:3: One day the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, came in and heard Khadija speaking with Fatima, peace be upon her. He said to her: O Khadija, with whom are you speaking?
22:4: She said: The child that is within me speaks to me and keeps me company. He said: O Khadija, this is Gabriel, who tells me that she is a girl,
22:5: and that she is the pure and blessed offspring; and that God, blessed and exalted, will make my progeny from her, and will make from her progeny the Imams, and will appoint them His successors in His earth after the ending of His revelation.
22:6: Khadija remained thus until her delivery drew near. Then she sent word to the women of Quraysh and of Banu Hashim: Come and attend me in what women do for women.
22:7: But they sent back to her: You disobeyed us and did not accept our word; you married Muhammad, the orphan of Abu Talib, a poor man with no wealth. So we shall not
23:0: come, nor attend to any part of your affair. Khadija, peace be upon her, was grieved at that — when four tawny women [14] came in upon her,
23:1: tall, as though they were of the women of Banu Hashim. She took fright at them when she saw them, and one of them said: Do not grieve, O Khadija, for we are the messengers of your Lord to you, and we are your sisters. I am Sara; and this is Asiya bint Muzahim, who is your companion in the Garden; and this is Maryam bint 'Imran; and this is Kulthum the sister of Musa b. 'Imran. God has sent us to you, to attend you in what women do for women. So one sat at her right, another at her left, the third before her and the fourth behind her; and she gave birth to Fatima, pure and purified.
23:2: When she came forth to the earth, a light shone from her until it entered the houses of Mecca, and there remained no place in the east of the earth or in its west but that light shone in it. And ten of the houris came in, each one of them with a basin from the Garden and an ewer from the Garden, and in the ewer was water from al-Kawthar. The woman who was before her took her and washed her with the water of al-Kawthar, and brought out two white cloths, whiter than milk and sweeter of scent than musk and ambergris; she wrapped her in one and veiled her with the second. Then she bade her speak, and Fatima uttered the two testimonies and said: I bear witness that there is no god but God,
23:3: and that my father is the Messenger of God, master of the prophets; and that my husband is the master of the legatees; and that my sons are the masters of the grandsons.
23:4: Then she greeted them, and named each one of them by her name, and they turned to her smiling. The houris rejoiced, and the people of heaven gave one another glad tidings of the birth of Fatima, peace be upon her; and there came to be in heaven a brilliant light that the angels had not seen before that. The women said: Take her, O Khadija — pure, purified, unsullied and blessed; blessed is she, and blessed is her progeny.
23:5: So she took her, glad and rejoicing, and gave her her breast, and it flowed for her. And Fatima, peace be upon her, would grow as a child grows in a month, and would grow in a month as a child grows in a year. [14]
23:6: (13) Samira samaratan: his colour was between black and white; samar. Aqrab al-Mawarid.
23:n14: Amali al-Saduq, p. 76; Bihar, vol. 43, p. 2, hadith 1.
24:0: Section [on the number of her names and the reason for her naming]. From Yunus b. Zabyan, who said: Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, said: Fatima has nine names with God, mighty and exalted — Fatima, al-Siddiqa, al-Mubaraka, al-Tahira, al-Zakiyya, al-Radiyya, al-Mardiyya, al-Muhaddatha and al-Zahra. Then he said: Do you know what the interpretation of Fatima is?
24:1: I said: Tell me, my master. He said: She was weaned away from evil. Then he said: Had the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, not married her, she would have had no match until the Day of Resurrection upon the face of the earth — Adam and those after him. [1]
24:2: And in a number of the traditions: she was named Fatima because she and her partisans were weaned away from the Fire; and that she was weaned by knowledge; and that she was weaned from menstruation; and that creation was weaned from the knowledge of her; and that God weaned her and her progeny from the Fire — whoever of them meets God professing His oneness and faith in His Messenger; and that God weaned from the Fire whoever loves her. [2]
24:3: And it is related that the name Fatima is drawn from the name of God, al-Fatir. She was named al-Tahira for her purity from every defilement and her purity from every obscenity; and she never saw a day of blood, nor lochia. [3]
24:n1: Bihar, vol. 43, p. 10, hadith 1; Dala'il al-Imama, p. 10.
24:n2: Bihar, vol. 43, pp. 12-13, hadiths 3, 4, 8, 9, 18; and also p. 65, hadith 58; and 'Ilal al-Shara'i', vol. 1, pp. 178-179.
25:0: And she was named al-Zahra because she would shine with light for the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, three times in the day. [4]
25:1: It is related from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari, who said: I asked the master of al-'Askar, peace be upon him: Why was Fatima named al-Zahra?
25:2: He said: Her face would shine for the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, at the beginning of the day like the sun in its brightness,
25:3: and at midday like the shining moon, and at the setting of the sun like the glittering star. [5]
25:4: Al-Saduq related from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida, peace be upon him, in a hadith, that he said: When the crescent of the month of Ramadan rose, the light of Fatima, peace be upon her, would overcome the crescent and it would be hidden; and when she was absent from it, it appeared. [6]
25:5: And from al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, who said: She was named al-Zahra because she has in the Garden a dome of red ruby, its height in the air a year's journey, suspended by the power of the Almighty — it has no tie above it to hold it, and no pillar beneath it to bear it. It has a hundred thousand gates, at every gate a thousand of the angels. The people of the Garden behold it as one of you beholds the glittering, shining star in the horizon of the sky, and they say: This is al-Zahra, which belongs to Fatima, God's blessings be upon her. [7]
25:6: And it is related in a report also that when God, mighty and exalted, wished to try the angels, He sent upon them a cloud of darkness, so that the angels could not see the first of them from the last of them, nor the last from the first. They asked God, glory be to Him, to lift it from them, and God Most High answered them: He created the light of Fatima al-Zahra that day like a lamp, and hung it upon the pendant of the Throne, and the seven heavens and the seven earths shone. It is for that reason that she was named al-Zahra.
25:7: And the angels were glorifying God and declaring Him holy; and God said: By My might
26:0: and My majesty, I shall surely make the reward of your glorification and your sanctification, until the Day of Resurrection, for those who love this woman and her father and her husband and her sons. (8)
26:1: Among her names also are al-Hasan (the chaste), al-Hurra (the free), al-Sayyida (the mistress), al-'Adhra' (the virgin), al-Hawra' (the houri), Maryam al-Kubra (the greater Mary), and al-Batul. [9]
26:2: It is related concerning the meaning of al-Batul that she is the one who never saw blood — that is, she did not menstruate — and that it was by this that Maryam, the mother of 'Isa, peace be upon them, was named. It has been said that al-batl is severance, and that Fatima was named al-Batul for her being set apart from the women of her time in excellence, in religion and in lineage; and it has been said, for her being cut off from the world towards God Most High; and it has been said, because she was set apart as having no peer. [10]
26:3: Ibn Shahrashub said in the Manaqib: It is established in the reports that Fatima has twenty names, each name indicating a virtue; Ibn Babawayh mentioned them in the book of the birth of Fatima, peace be upon her. [11]
26:4: [Section on her kunyas.] As for her kunyas, God's blessings be upon her: Umm al-Hasan, Umm al-Husayn, Umm al-Muhassin, Umm al-A'imma, Umm Abiha, and Umm al-Mu'minin — this last kunya occurring in her ziyara. And in the Manaqib it is said that she is called in heaven al-Nuriyya, al-Samawiyya, al-Haniya.
26:5: I say: al-Haniya is she who is tender towards her husband and her children.
26:6: As for her tenderness towards her husband, it is enough in that to recall what came upon her of beating and humiliation, the breaking of the rib, and the mark of the whip upon her arm like an armlet — the details of which will come, God Most High willing. (1) Irshad, p. 403; Bihar, vol. 43, p. 17.
27:0: all of that being in the protection of her husband, until she died a martyr. And with all that, when death came upon her she wept, and the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said to her: My lady, what makes you weep?
27:1: She said: I weep for what you will meet after me. He said to her: Do not weep, for by God, that is a small thing to me in the cause of God Most High. [12]
27:2: Al-Shaykh al-Mufid related in the Irshad that when the Prophet sent the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon them both, to the raid of Dhat al-Raml — which is also called the raid of Dhat al-Salasil — the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, had a headband which he would not bind on until the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, sent him upon some hard undertaking. So he went to the house of Fatima, peace be upon her, and sought the headband from her. She said: Where are you bound, and where has my father sent you?
27:3: He said: To the valley of the sands. And she wept out of tenderness for him. The Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, came in while she was in that state and said to her: What ails you, that you weep? Do you fear that your husband will be slain?
27:4: By no means, God willing. And 'Ali, peace be upon him, said to him: Do not begrudge me the Garden, O Messenger of God. [13]
27:5: As for her tenderness towards her children, it is enough in that to recall what al-Saduq related from Hammad, from al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, who said: It is not lawful for anyone to join in marriage two of the children of Fatima, peace be upon her; that reaches her, and it grieves her. I said: It reaches her? He said: Yes, by God. [14]
27:6: The author of 'Umdat al-Talib said, in the course of the circumstances of the Banu Dawud b. Musa al-Hasani: The Banu Dawud b. Musa have a notable tale, well known among the genealogists and others and furnished with a chain, which is mentioned in the Diwan of Ibn 'Unayn. It is that Abu al-Mahasin Nasr Allah b. 'Unayn al-Dimashqi the poet set out for Mecca, may God Most High ennoble it, having with him money and cloth. Some of the Banu Dawud came out against him, took what he had, stripped him and wounded him. So he wrote to al-Malik al-'Aziz b. Ayyub
27:n13: Irshad, pp. 60-61. His words, peace be upon him, “Do not begrudge me the Garden”: that is, do not be niggardly — meaning, leave me, that I may be slain in the way of God and attain martyrdom.
28:0: the lord of Yemen. His brother al-Malik al-Nasir had sent to him, summoning him to settle on the coast that had been wrested from the hands of the Franks; but Ibn 'Unayn made the coast seem of little worth to him and made Yemen desirable to him, and incited him against the Sharifs who had done to him what they did. The opening of the ode: — The descriptions of your eloquent bounty have worn out the tongue, and in generosity you have passed the bound of the fair and the excellent. — Say not, “the coast of the Franks, I shall take it”; for it is worth nothing, set beside Aden. — And if you desire holy war, then let your sword part from a people who have squandered God's ordinances and the sunnas. — Purify with your sword the House of God from defilement, and from the baseness and the foulness of certain folk within it. — And say not, “they are the children of Fatima”; had they met the House of Harb, they would have made war on al-Hasan. — He said: When he had spoken this ode, he saw in his sleep Fatima al-Zahra, peace be upon her, circling the House. He greeted her, and she did not answer him; so he humbled himself and abased himself, and asked what his sin was that had required the withholding of her greeting. And al-Zahra, peace be upon her, recited to him:
28:1: Far be it from the sons of Fatima, all of them, that baseness should be shown of them, or foulness. — It is only the days, in their excusing and their evil doing, that have done ill by us. — Where is the wrong of one single child of mine, that you have made all reviling ours, deliberately?
29:0: So repent to God; for whoever commits a sin against us, he is forgiven what he has perpetrated. — Show honour for the sake of the eye of al-Mustafa, their grandfather, and do not despise any eyes of his Family. — For whatever reaches you from them, you will meet from us, on the Day of Gathering, with what is pleasant. — Abu al-Mahasin Nasr Allah b. 'Unayn said: I awoke from my sleep, alarmed and terrified, and God had completed my recovery from the wound and the sickness. So I wrote down these verses and committed them to memory, and I repented to God Most High of what I had said, and I cut that ode away.
29:1: An excuse offered to the daughter of the Prophet of guidance: overlook the sin of an evildoer who has transgressed, — and a repentance you may accept from a brother whose speech cast him into distress. — By God, were one of them to cut me down with the sword of oppression or with the spear, — I would not see what he does as evil; rather I would see him, in the deed, to have done well. [15]
30:0: Chapter Two: on her merit, her majesty, her asceticism, her worship, her knowledge, the nobility of her character, and the love the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, bore her. Section. Fatima, God's blessings be upon her, was of the People of the Cloak, of the Mubahala, and of those who migrated in the hardest of times. She was among those concerning whom the verse of Purification was revealed; Gabriel took pride in being counted of them; and God bore witness to their truthfulness. To her belongs the motherhood of the Imams, peace be upon them, and the posterity of the Messenger, may God bless him and his Family, until the Day of Resurrection. She is the Mistress of the Women of the Worlds, of the first of them and of the last.
30:1: She was the most like of all people to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, in speech and in discourse; her nature told of his nature, and her walk did not depart from his walk. When she came in to him he would welcome her, kiss her hands and seat her in his own place; and when he came in to her she would rise to him, welcome him and kiss his hands.
30:2: The Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, would kiss her often, and whenever he longed for the scent of the Garden he would smell her scent. He used to say: “Fatima is a part of me; whoever gladdens her has gladdened me, and whoever grieves her has grieved me. Fatima is the dearest of people to me.” [1] — besides other things that disclose the abundance of his love, may God bless him and his Family,
31:0: for her — such as his calling her “O beloved of her father”.
31:1: As al-Tabari the Imami related from Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, from Fatima, peace be upon her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, said: O beloved of her father, every intoxicant is forbidden, and every intoxicant is wine. [2] And let it be known that it has been established in its place that the love of those brought near for their children, their kin and their beloved ones does not arise from the motives of the self or from human appetites. Rather they have divested themselves of all of that and made their love and their will purely for God; they love nothing but God Most High, and their love for what is other than Him goes back only to their love for Him.
31:2: It is for this reason that Ya'qub, peace be upon him, did not love any of his other children as he loved Yusuf, peace be upon him. They, in their ignorance of the cause of his love, ascribed him to error and said: We are a band, and we are more deserving to be loved by him, for we are strong to carry through what he wishes of the affairs of the world. But his abundant love for Yusuf was only for God Most High's love of him and His choosing of him — and the beloved of the beloved is beloved.
31:3: Al-Shaykh al-Kulayni, may God perfume his grave, related from Muhammad b. Sinan, who said: I was with Abu Ja'far the Second, peace be upon him, and I raised the matter of the disagreement of the Shi'a. He said: O Muhammad, God, blessed and exalted, was ever alone in His oneness; then He created Muhammad, 'Ali and Fatima, God's blessings be upon them, and they remained a thousand ages. Then He created all things and made them witnesses of their creation, and made obedience to them binding upon them, and committed their affairs to them. So they make lawful what they will [and make unlawful what they will], and they will not will save that God, blessed and exalted, wills. Then he said: O Muhammad, this is the religion: whoever goes on ahead of it has left it, whoever falls behind it is destroyed, and whoever keeps to it is joined. Take it to yourself, O Muhammad. [3]
31:4: I say: it appears from this noble hadith that Fatima, God's blessings be upon her, is among those to whom God Most High committed the affairs of all things; so she makes lawful what she will and makes unlawful what she will.
31:n3: Al-Kafi, vol. 1, p. 441, hadith 5; Bihar, vol. 25, p. 340.
32:0: It has come in many traditions from the Imams, peace be upon them, that “with them is the Mushaf of Fatima, God's blessings be upon her”.
32:1: In al-Safi, from Basa'ir al-Darajat, he said: Fatima left behind a mushaf which is not the Qur'an, but a speech from the speech of God which He sent down to her — the dictation of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, and the hand of the Commander of the Faithful 'Ali, peace be upon him. [4]
32:2: And from Abu Basir, who said: I came in to Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, and said: May I be your ransom, I wish to ask you about a matter; [may I be your ransom, is there] anyone here who may hear my words? He said: Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, raised a curtain between himself and another room and looked into it, then said: O Abu Muhammad, ask whatever has occurred to you. I said: May I be your ransom, your partisans relate that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, taught 'Ali, peace be upon him, a gate from which a thousand gates are opened!
32:3: He said: O Abu Muhammad, by God, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, taught 'Ali, peace be upon him, a thousand gates, from each of which a thousand gates are opened. I said to him: By God, this is knowledge indeed!
32:4: He said: He scratched in the earth a while, then said: It is knowledge, yet it is not that. Then he said: O Abu Muhammad, with us is al-Jami'a — and what do they know what al-Jami'a is? I said: May I be your ransom, and what is al-Jami'a? He said: A scroll seventy cubits long, by the cubit of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, of his dictation from the parting of his lips [5] and in the hand of 'Ali, peace be upon him, with his right hand. In it is every lawful thing and every unlawful thing, and everything of which people have need, down to the indemnity for a scratch. And he struck me with his hand and said: Will you permit me, O Abu Muhammad?
32:5: I said: May I be your ransom, I am yours; do what you will. He said: So he pinched me with his hand and said: Even the indemnity for this — as though he were angered. I said: May I be your ransom,
32:n5: That is, the parting of his lips.
33:0: by God, this is knowledge indeed! He said: It is knowledge, yet it is not that.
33:1: Then he said: And with us is al-Jafr — and what do they know what al-Jafr is? I said: And what is al-Jafr?
33:2: He said: A vessel of red leather, in which is the knowledge of the prophets and of the legatees, and the knowledge of the scholars who passed away from among the Children of Israel. I said: This indeed is knowledge. He said: It is knowledge, yet it is not that.
33:3: Then he was silent a while, then said: And with us is the Mushaf of Fatima, peace be upon her — and what do they know what the Mushaf of Fatima, peace be upon her, is? I said: And what is the Mushaf of Fatima, peace be upon her?
33:4: He said: A mushaf containing three times the like of this Qur'an of yours. By God, there is not in it a single letter of your Qur'an; [it is only something God dictated and revealed to her]. I said: By God, this is knowledge! He said: It is knowledge, yet it is not that.
33:5: Then he was silent a while, then said: With us is the knowledge of what has been and the knowledge of what will be, until the Hour arises. I said: May I be your ransom, by God, this indeed is knowledge! He said: It is knowledge, yet it is not that. I said: May I be your ransom, then what thing is knowledge?
33:6: He said: What occurs by night and by day, matter after matter and thing after thing, until the Day of Resurrection. [6]
33:7: And in a number of the traditions she, peace be upon her, is one of the four riders on the Day of Resurrection: she rides al-'Adba', the she-camel of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family. [7]
33:8: Ibn Shahrashub related that when death came upon the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, the she-camel said: To whom do you entrust me after you?
33:9: He said: O 'Adba', God bless you; you belong to my daughter Fatima, God's blessings be upon her — you shall carry her in this world and in the next. And when the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, was taken, she came to Fatima, peace be upon her, by night and said: Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Messenger of God; the hour of my parting from the world has come. By God, I have taken pleasure in neither fodder nor drink after the Messenger of God, may God bless
33:n7: Al-Khisal of al-Saduq, may God have mercy on him, p. 186.
34:0: him and his Family. And she died three days after the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family. [8]
34:1: And from the Tafsir of Furat b. Ibrahim, from the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, came in one day upon Fatima, peace be upon her, and she was sorrowful. He said to her — and he carried the hadith on concerning the states of the Resurrection, until he said: And when you reach the gate of the Garden, twelve thousand houris will meet you, who have met none before you and will meet none after you, in their hands spears of light, upon riding-camels of light whose housings are of yellow gold and red ruby and whose reins are of moist pearl, upon every camel a covering of layered silk brocade. And when you enter the Garden its people will rejoice at you, and tables of jewel upon pillars of light will be set out for your partisans; they will eat from them while the people are still at the Reckoning, and they will abide in what their souls desire. And when the friends of God are settled in the Garden, Adam will visit you, and the prophets after him — the report. [9]
34:2: And it is related from her, peace be upon her, who said: When there was revealed “Do not make the calling of the Messenger among you like your calling of one another”, I stood in awe of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, to say to him “father”, and I would say “O Messenger of God”. He turned from me once, and twice, and three times; then he came to me and said: O Fatima, it was not revealed concerning you, nor concerning your family, nor your progeny. You are of me and I am of you. It was revealed only concerning the people of harshness and roughness among Quraysh, the people of pomp and pride. Say “father”, for it is more quickening to the heart and more pleasing to the Lord. [10]
34:3: And from Misbah al-Anwar, from the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, from Fatima, peace be upon her: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, said to me: “Whoever invokes blessing upon you, God Most High forgives him, and joins him to me wherever I am in the Garden.” [11]
34:n10: Tafsir Nur al-Thaqalayn, vol. 3, p. 629; al-Burhan, vol. 3, p. 154.
35:0: Al-Kulayni, from Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, from Jabir b. 'Abd Allah al-Ansari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, went out making for Fatima, peace be upon her, and I was with him. When we came to the door he put his hand upon it and pushed it, then said: Peace be upon you. Fatima, peace be upon her, said: Upon you be peace, O Messenger of God. He said: May I enter?
35:1: She said: Enter, O Messenger of God. He said: May I enter, and whoever is with me?
35:2: She said: O Messenger of God, I have no head-covering. He said: O Fatima, take the surplus of your wrapper and cover your head with it. So she did. Then he said: Peace be upon you. She said: And upon you be peace, O Messenger of God. He said: May I enter?
35:3: She said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: I, and whoever is with me?
35:4: She said: You, and whoever is with you. Jabir said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, entered, and I entered; and behold, the face of Fatima, peace be upon her, was yellow, as though it were the belly of a locust. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, said: How is it that I see your face yellow?
35:5: She said: O Messenger of God, it is hunger. So he said: “O God, who satisfies hunger and wards off ruin, satisfy Fatima the daughter of Muhammad” — and so on. [12]
35:6: And from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon him, rose one day hungry and said: O Fatima, have you anything to feed me? She said: No, by Him who honoured my father with prophethood and honoured you with the legateeship, there has been nothing with me this morning; nor has there been anything we have eaten these two days past but something with which I preferred you over myself and over these two sons of mine, al-Hasan and al-Husayn. 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: O Fatima, why did you not tell me, that I might seek something for you? She said: O Abu al-Hasan, I am ashamed before my God to burden your soul with what it has no power over. [13]
35:7: And from Qurb al-Isnad, from Abu 'Abd Allah, from his father, peace be upon him, who said: 'Ali and Fatima, God's blessings be upon them, brought a dispute before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, concerning the household service;
35:n12: Al-Kafi, vol. 5, p. 528, the Book of Marriage.
35:n13: Bihar, vol. 43, p. 59, quoting Tafsir al-Furat.
36:0: and he, may God bless him and his Family, ruled for Fatima, peace be upon her, the service of what lay within the door, and ruled for 'Ali, peace be upon him, what lay beyond it. He said: Fatima, God's blessings be upon her, said: None knows the joy that entered me but God, at the Messenger of God's sparing me the burden of dealing with the necks of men. [14]
36:1: From al-Khara'ij, it is related that Salman, may God be pleased with him, said: Fatima, peace be upon her, was seated with a hand-mill before her, grinding barley with it, and upon the handle of the mill was flowing blood; and al-Husayn, peace be upon him, was in a corner of the house writhing from hunger. I said: O daughter of the Messenger of God, your hands are worn raw — and here is Fidda. She, peace be upon her, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, charged me that the service should be hers for a day; and yesterday was the day of her service. Salman said: I said: I am a freedman of your manumission — shall I grind the barley, or quiet al-Husayn, peace be upon him, for you?
36:2: She said: I am the gentler at quieting him; you grind the barley. So I ground some of the barley, and then the call to prayer was given; so I went and prayed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family. When I had finished I told 'Ali, peace be upon him, what I had seen, and he wept and went out; then he returned and smiled, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, asked him about that.
36:3: He said: I came in upon Fatima, and she was lying upon her back with al-Husayn asleep upon her breast, and before her a mill turning with no hand upon it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, smiled and said: O 'Ali, do you not know that God has angels who travel about the earth serving Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad until the Hour arises? [15]
36:4: And it is related that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, came in upon 'Ali, peace be upon him, and found him and Fatima, peace be upon her, grinding at the hand-mill. The Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, said: Which of you two is the more weary?
36:5: 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: Fatima, O Messenger of God. So he said to her: Rise, my little daughter. And she rose,
36:n15: Bihar, vol. 43, p. 28; al-Khara'ij, vol. 2, p. 530.
37:0: and the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, sat in her place with 'Ali, peace be upon him, and took his share with him in the grinding. [16]
37:1: And from certain of the books of the Manaqib, from Jabir b. 'Abd Allah: The Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, remained some days without tasting food, until that grew hard upon him. He went round the dwellings of his wives and found nothing with any one of them. So he came to Fatima, peace be upon her, and said: My little daughter, have you anything I may eat, for I am hungry?
37:2: She said: No, by God — may my father and my mother be your ransom. When he had gone out from her, a neighbour of hers sent her two loaves and a piece of meat. She took it from her and put it in a bowl of hers and covered it over, and said: I shall surely prefer the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, with it over myself and over those who are with me — and they were all in need of a fill of food. So she sent al-Hasan, or al-Husayn, to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, and he returned to her. She said: May my father and my mother be your ransom, God has brought us something, and I have put it away. He said: Bring it. So she brought it to him and uncovered the bowl, and behold, it was filled with bread and meat. When she looked at it she was astounded, and knew that it was an honour from God, mighty and exalted; so she praised God and invoked blessing upon His prophet. He, may God bless him and his Family, said: Whence is this to you, my little daughter?
37:3: She said: It is from God; truly God provides for whom He will without reckoning. So he praised God, mighty and exalted, and said: Praise belongs to God, who has made you like the mistress of the women of the worlds among the women of the Children of Israel in their time; for when God Most High provided for her and she was asked about it, she would say: It is from God; truly God provides for whom He will without reckoning.
37:4: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, sent for 'Ali, peace be upon him; and the Messenger of God, 'Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, peace be upon them, and all the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, and the people of his house — all ate and were satisfied, and the bowl remained as it was. Fatima, peace be upon her, said: And I gave abundantly from it to all my neighbours, and God placed in it blessing and good, as God did with Maryam. [17]
38:0: Section [on the abundance of her worship]. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: There was in this community none more devoted in worship than Fatima, peace be upon her; she would stand in prayer until her feet swelled. [1]
38:1: And the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, said to her: What thing is best for a woman?
38:2: She said: That she should not see a man, nor a man see her. So he drew her to himself and said: “Offspring, one of another.” [2]
38:3: And al-Hasan b. 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: I saw my mother Fatima, peace be upon her, standing in her prayer-niche on the eve of her Friday, and she did not cease bowing and prostrating until the pillar of dawn broke. And I heard her praying for the believing men and the believing women, naming them and praying much for them, and not praying for herself in anything. I said to her: Mother, why do you not pray for yourself as you pray for others? She said: My little son, the neighbour first, then the household. [3]
38:4: And al-Saduq related from Fatima, God's blessings be upon her, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, say: In Friday there is an hour such that no Muslim man happens upon it, asking God, mighty and exalted, in it for some good, but that He gives it to him. She said: I said: O Messenger of God, which hour is it?
38:5: He said: When half the disc of the sun has inclined towards setting. He said: And Fatima, peace be upon her, would say to her servant: Climb up on the rise, and when you see half the disc of the sun inclining towards setting, tell me, that I may supplicate. [4]
38:6: And it is related that she, peace be upon her, when she stood in her prayer-niche, her light would shine for the people of heaven as the light of the stars shines for the people of the earth. [5]
38:n3: 'Ilal al-Shara'i', vol. 1, p. 182; Bihar, vol. 43, p. 82.
38:n4: Wasa'il al-Shi'a, vol. 3, the chapters on the Friday prayer and its etiquette, p. 69. Al-dirab is the small hill; perhaps what is meant here is the raised part of it.
39:0: And al-Saduq, may God have mercy on him, related from the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, that he said to a man of Banu Sa'd: Shall I not tell you of myself and of Fatima? She was with me, and she was among the dearest of his family to him. She drew water with the waterskin until it left a mark upon her breast; she ground with the hand-mill until her hands were calloused; she swept the house until her clothes were dusty; and she kindled the fire beneath the pot until her clothes were blackened. From that she suffered severe harm.
39:1: I said to her: Were you to go to your father and ask him for a servant, to spare you the hardship of the work you are in — so she went to the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, and found people in conversation with him; and she was ashamed, and turned back.
39:2: He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, knew that she had come for a need. He said: And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, came to us in the morning while we were in our wrap.
39:3: He said: Peace be upon you. And we kept silent, being ashamed of our situation. Then he said: Peace be upon you. And we kept silent. Then he said: Peace be upon you. And we feared that if we did not answer him he would turn away — for he used to do that: he would greet three times, and if he were given leave he entered, and otherwise he turned away. So I said: And upon you be peace, O Messenger of God; enter. And he did no more than sit at our heads, and said: O Fatima, what was your need yesterday with Muhammad, may God bless him and his Family?
39:4: He, peace be upon him, said: I feared that if we did not answer him he would rise. He said: So I put out my head and said: By God, I shall tell you, O Messenger of God. She drew water with the waterskin until it left a mark upon her breast; she pulled at the hand-mill until her hands were calloused; she swept the house until her clothes were dusty; and she kindled the fire beneath the pot until her clothes were blackened. And I said to her: Were you to go to your father and ask him for a servant, to spare you the hardship of the work you are in.
39:5: He, may God bless him and his Family, said: Shall I not teach you both something better for you than a servant?
39:6: When you take to your bed, glorify God thirty-three times, praise Him thirty-three times, and magnify Him thirty-four times. He said: And she, peace be upon her, put out her head and said: I am content with God and with His Messenger — three times over. [6]
39:n6: 'Ilal al-Shara'i', p. 366; Bihar, vol. 43, p. 82. Majilat yaduha: that is, the skin of her hand thickened from the work. Dakina al-thawb: when it is soiled and its colour turns dusty. Al-lifa': a garment in which the body is wholly wrapped. Hudathan: that is, a company in conversation. Wa lam ya'ud an jalasa: that is, he did no more than sit.
